Amy Chen: Quick sync — call out: large ecommerce customer asked for a 'microguard' feature: small, guaranteed soft reservations for short spikes (30s-5m) that don't affect their reserved pool billing. Wants graceful fallthrough to shared pools without 429s.
Sanjay Rao: Interesting—so a transient reservation layer in front of reserved pools. Do they expect billing for microguard separately?
Amy Chen: They want it free within a small quota per month (like 500 short guards), otherwise charged if over. Main ask is availability during flash sales.
Marco Li: Implementation sketch: a token-bucket per tenant for microguard, enforced at admission. If bucket >0 -> serve from reserved pool with priority flag. If empty -> fallthrough policy: 1) try shared dedicated lane, 2) degrade to best-effort spot, 3) if nothing -> 429.
Priya Patel: Important: SLA implications. If we surface microguard as "guaranteed" we need clear SLOs. Suggest we label it "soft-guard" and include measured p95 latency for microguard hits.
Amy Chen: Agreed. Product proposal: soft-guard = short reservation; launch criteria: acceptance tests with 5 customer pilots, no more than 1% additional latency at P95, billing/usage UI + docs.
Sanjay Rao: Ops questions: autoscale interplay. If many microguard hits spike, do we auto-scale reserved pool? probably not automatically — we should throttle microguard by tenant token bucket and have a global cap to avoid cascade autoscaling.
Marco Li: Implementation detail: add a microguard admission tier that is accounted separately in the autoscale estimator. Autoscale only considers steady traffic plus confirmed reserved usage; microguard contributes to a short-term headroom signal but capped.
Priya Patel: Prioritization: where does this fit on roadmap? Customer asked for pilot in 6 weeks. We have Dedicated backlog full. My suggestion: carve a scoped MVP: API flag + admission tier + metrics + billing flag and run pilot without autoscale coupling. That should be 3 sprint work for infra + 1 sprint for product/docs.
Amy Chen: MVP acceptance criteria checklist: 1) admission flag accepted and enforced; 2) token-bucket usage metrics surfaced in Console; 3) customer pilot with defined traffic pattern passes (no 429s for valid microguard hits); 4) billing event emitted for overage.
Sanjay Rao: Risks: 1) unbounded demand causing hot nodes; 2) complexity in fallback ordering; 3) support burden to explain when microguard doesn't fire. Mitigations: global hard cap, default fallback order documented, support playbook + automated incident signature tagging.
Marco Li: Dev tasks I see: a) admission hook + priority bit b) token-bucket service c) console usage panel d) simulator for spike tests e) integration test for fallthrough order. Estimate 5 eng-weeks infra + 3 eng-weeks console.
Priya Patel: OK — product decision to prioritize behind the current Dedicated prewarm work but ahead of non-critical UX polish. I'll slot as "customer pilot" item in next planning cycle and pair an SE to run pilot.
Amy Chen: Action items: Priya -> draft pilot SOW by Tue; Marco -> prototype admission hook PR by EOD Fri (branch feature/microguard); Sanjay -> define autoscale cap knobs and emergency drain playbook. CapacityBot: scheduled bump: reminder to run canary simulation on 1768460000.
Amy Chen: Thanks — will update the roadmap doc and ping legal for billing language. :thumbsup:
